# EARLY TREATMENT OF INFLUENZA AS AN ALTERNATIVE TO CHEMOPROPHYLAXIS

In most cases, if a person is suspected of having been exposed to influenza,

early treatment, should signs or symptoms develop, is preferred rather than

chemoprophylaxis.

The provider should explain the early signs and symptoms of influenza to the

patient and advise the patient to immediately contact a health care provider for

evaluation and possible early treatment if these symptoms or signs develop.

Influenza-like symptoms or signs include fever, cough, sore throat, runny or

stuffy nose, body aches, headache, chills, fatigue, vomiting, and diarrhea.

Influenza can present without fever.

Health care providers should use clinical judgment regarding situations where

early recognition of illness and treatment might be an appropriate alternative

to chemoprophylaxis.

# Early treatment alternative or chemoprophylaxis may be considered:

*Persons who are part of a high-risk group and are household or close contacts

of someone with influenza-like illness Chemoprophylaxis duration: 7 days after

last known exposure

# Chemoprophylaxis recommended:

*For control of outbreaks in institutional settings (long-term care facilities

and hospitals)

Chemoprophylaxis duration: minimum of 2 weeks and continuing up to 1 week after

the last known case is identified.

Note: Antiviral chemoprophylaxis is recommended for all residents, including

those who have received influenza vaccination.

# Chemoprophylaxis considered:

*Atypical situations (such as case clusters). Contact the state health

department for consultation.

# Antiviral Prophylaxis Recommendations

Preferred:

[Oseltamivir 75 mg po q24h R](psozid2-oseltamivir-75-mg-po-qday-prophy-14-days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid3-oseltamivir-75-mg-po-qday-14d-prophy)

(See information above for length of prophylaxis)

# **Below is for information only, quick orders are not available

Alternative treatment:

Zanamivir is not recommended for patients with chronic respiratory diseases such

as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. These patients may have

bronchospasm with zanamivir. If zanamivir must be used, and patients are using

an inhaled bronchodilator, zanamivir should be taken just after the

bronchodilator.

Requires Infectious Disease Approval

Zanamivir 2 inhalations (2 x 5 mg)daily [O] (see above for duration of

prophylaxis)
